Most people probably don't know this (and I can't pretend I didn't know it either), but Apple has actually published extremely detailed dimensional drawings for dozens of devices, so that accessory manufacturers can design their products accordingly. Here are the details.

Apple hardware, rendered in painstaking detail

For nearly three decades, Jason Kottke has been one of my main sources for interesting content online (and beyond), and there are so many things I definitely would never have discovered if it weren't for him.

A few days ago, he posted this article, with a link to the "Dimensional Drawings" section of the Accessories area on the Apple Developer website.

Put simply, this is a repository containing extremely detailed technical drawings covering a total of 96 devices at present, including the newly released iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, as well as the AirPods 5.

The list also includes products like the MacBook Neo and Siri Remote, as well as accessories like the AirTag, AirPods charging case, and even the ZEISS lens accessories for Apple Vision Pro.

Each document contains precise dimensions for every part of the device, from overall size and curvature, to buttons, cameras, sensors, speakers and ports, along with detailed "keepout zones" and instructions indicating where certain materials must not be placed.

Although these documents were originally intended for accessory manufacturers, they should also be fascinating to anyone with even a passing interest in hardware and industrial design, or simply for those who appreciate that meticulous, exacting style of Apple products.

To view Apple's dimensional drawings, please click this link. If you haven't yet followed kottke.org, be sure to start following it right away.
